summary.text: CA9 has the strongest convergent evidence and is the most robust call in the whole analysis. It is first in the overall convergence ranking and stays in the top ten under most random re-weightings [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:convergence:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=convergence; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.894]. The protein is clearly higher in tumour than in normal kidney [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2686], almost all of its tumour transcripts come from the cancer cells themselves [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], and the antibody girentuximab has a clinical-development record. CA9 is best read as an antigen for antibodies, imaging and conjugates and as a tissue biomarker, not as a functional dependency: no ccRCC cell line depends on it, and expression is patchy in some tumours [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=24.3%].

A second tier of tumour-up surface or enzyme targets follows, each with a specific weakness. NNMT is made by tumour cells, its protein increase replicates in the independent confirmatory cohort [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=4.776], and higher expression goes with shorter overall survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301], but it has no clinical drug and no cell-line dependency. CD70 already has clinical antibodies, but a large part of its transcripts come from immune cells [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]. SCARB1 tops the target profile with a narrow rank interval [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.968], yet one single-cell dataset assigns it mainly to myeloid cells [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); li2022_tumour_cell_share=0.336]. EPAS1 (HIF-2 alpha, belzutifan) remains the only clinically validated axis and the only candidate with a selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3], even though its bulk expression signal is weak.

The strongest biomarker calls are genes lost in the tumour, which mark the loss of normal proximal-tubule metabolism. PSAT1 is the most robust biomarker in the analysis [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.986], and its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort [gene=PSAT1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-3.946]. The same holds for PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]. These genes are tissue-state biomarkers, not drug targets. Replication also removes candidates: the HK2 protein increase seen in discovery is not seen in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-0.256].

Unexplored candidates. The convergence ranking rewards literature and existing drugs, so little-studied genes come from the separate discovery screen, where 'novel' means few ccRCC papers and no clinical drug, not that nothing has been published. The two best candidates belong to the tumour-cell track and are identified and prioritised for experimental validation. COL23A1, a transmembrane collagen, is made mainly by the cancer cells [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. Its protein is higher in tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; protein_log2fc=2.512], the rise replicates in TCGA and survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], and it has antibody tractability with little vital-organ RNA. RAB42, a small GTPase, is also tumour-cell derived [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627] and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], but its surface annotation is doubtful. For both genes several things are still missing: staining of the protein in normal tissues, proof of an accessible surface epitope, a selective dependency (neither has one), confirmatory-cohort protein data and a measure of heterogeneity across tumour cells. Immunohistochemistry on tumour and normal tissue microarrays, followed by knockdown and antibody-binding studies in ccRCC models, would test them. The leading immune-track gene, GAL3ST4, is a macrophage gene whose signal largely disappears at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], so it is a microenvironment hypothesis. Nothing here shows that treating any of these genes would help a patient, and the literature agent found no earlier preclinical ccRCC work on them in the corpus.

omics.text: At the protein level, the tumour-up candidates are CA9 [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2686], CD70 [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.4207], NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709], SLC16A3 (MCT4) [gene=SLC16A3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.2792], SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.8371] and ENPP3 [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.5438]. RNA agrees in direction for all of them. SLC16A3 and SLC2A1 (GLUT1) together describe the glycolytic, HIF-driven programme of ccRCC, and they read better as mechanism than as selective targets.

The strongest losses are metabolic enzymes of the normal tubule: PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.9635], PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.8592] and ALDH6A1. They separate tumour from normal tissue well, which makes them biomarkers, but loss of a normal-tissue enzyme gives nothing to inhibit. Most of the top of the overall convergence ranking (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD, FABP1, NPHS2, PIGR) is this same tubule-loss signal.

literature.text: The literature supports CA9, CD70 and NNMT most directly. For CA9 it reports tumour-cell enrichment with low normal-kidney background and proof-of-concept CA9 PET imaging. For CD70 it reports overexpression with minimal normal-tissue expression, and CD70-specific radiotracer antibodies. For NNMT it reports upregulation linked to worse survival in one study, together with selective NNMT inhibitor chemistry that was not tested in ccRCC. COXFA4L2 (NDUFA4L2) has the densest mechanistic literature (hypoxia-induced, glycolytic, anti-ferroptotic), but all of it is preclinical. The VHL and HIF-2 alpha axis appears only through sentence-level support, including the belzutifan approval.

The literature is silent on several data-strong candidates: SCARB1 and ENPP3 have no extracted ccRCC relations, so they are data-supported candidates still waiting for literature. Three conflicts are flagged. PFKP is tumour-up, yet low expression was linked to poor survival. MT1G is lower in tumours, yet high expression within tumours is adverse. ABAT is tumour-suppressive, yet carries an approved inhibitor in the drug layer. Most claims rest on one or two bioinformatic papers.

external.text: Open Targets and DepMap split the candidates into two groups. Surface antigens with clinical-stage biologics (CA9 with girentuximab, CD70 with cusatuzumab, ENPP3 with the conjugate AGS-16C3F) show no ccRCC cell-line dependency, so any benefit would come from antibody, imaging or conjugate delivery rather than loss of function. EPAS1 is the only candidate with a selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3] and an approved drug (belzutifan). VHL is the dominant driver, mutated in close to half of patients [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=0.4834]. It is a mechanism and stratification marker, not a direct target.

cells.text: Single-cell attribution separates tumour-intrinsic candidates from microenvironment genes. CA9 [gene=CA9; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.976], MET [gene=MET; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.935] and EGFR [gene=EGFR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.948] are carried by the cancer cells. KDR is endothelial [gene=KDR; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Endothelial; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.951]. CD74 and CXCR4 are immune-cell genes. EPAS1 transcripts sit mostly outside the cancer cells [gene=EPAS1; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=RCC; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.051], although droplet dropout limits this reading. KDR, CD74 and CXCR4 are therefore not tumour-intrinsic, even when bulk omics ranks them.

A second single-cell dataset confirms the cell of origin for CA9 [gene=CA9; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.981] and NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.948]. It does not confirm SCARB1, whose dominant source switches from myeloid cells to tumour cells between datasets [gene=SCARB1; type=sc_replication; source=Zhang et al. 2021 ccRCC single-cell RNA-seq (CZ CELLxGENE); zhang2021_tumour_cell_share=0.582]. The tumour-cell attribution of SCARB1, the leader of the target profile, is therefore unresolved.

spatial.text: In Visium sections, the composition-corrected in-situ source of CA9 is the tumour cells [gene=CA9; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.0.composition_corrected_share=0.999]. High-CA9 spots sit among other tumour spots [gene=CA9; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; enriched_neighbors.0.log2_enrichment=0.381] and, more weakly, near macrophages. KDR is the opposite case, with almost no in-situ contribution from tumour cells [gene=KDR; type=spatial_summary; source=DATASET:LI2022-VISIUM; in_situ_expressers.1.composition_corrected_share=0.002]. The spatial estimates depend on deconvolution and support the single-cell attributions rather than adding new candidates.

structure.text: Structural context comes from computationally detected cavities in predicted AlphaFold monomers. It is a descriptive heuristic only and is not evidence of a degron, of ligase compatibility or of degradability. No curated experimental degron or ternary-complex reference was used for these candidates. The CA9 model has a moderate top cavity [gene=CA9; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.546], and detected cavities cover part of its known experimental ligand contacts [gene=CA9; type=ligand_site_validation; source=PDBe-KB ligand sites (experimental holo structures); recall=0.5]. GAL3ST4 has the highest score among the candidates examined [gene=GAL3ST4; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.7874]. The COL23A1 model is low confidence [gene=COL23A1; type=alphafold_model; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; mean_plddt=58.91] with only a tiny cavity, so an antibody against an extracellular domain is the more plausible modality.

discovery.text: COL23A1 is a transmembrane collagen and the leading tumour-track candidate. The cancer cells make most of its tumour transcripts [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881]. It is strongly higher in TCGA tumours [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=5.8291], and the rise survives extrapolation to a pure tumour [gene=COL23A1; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.88], so it is not infiltration. It has no adverse prognosis [gene=COL23A1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.123], antibody and protein tractability, and low vital-organ RNA. What is missing is a selective dependency, normal-tissue protein staining and a measure of heterogeneity across tumour cells. Its literature is counted by gene symbol, so it is a data-ranked hypothesis.

RAB42 is a small Rab GTPase and the second tumour-track candidate. Cancer cells carry most of its transcripts [gene=RAB42; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.627]. It is higher in TCGA [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=4.371] and holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189], with no prognostic signal [gene=RAB42; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.058]. Its surface or secreted annotation is doubtful for an intracellular GTPase, so antibody access needs checking, and there is no dependency evidence.

The stroma and immune tracks give microenvironment hypotheses, not tumour-cell targets. OLFML2A is a fibroblast gene [gene=OLFML2A; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Fibroblast; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.647] that holds at full purity [gene=OLFML2A; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=1.527]. GAL3ST4 is a macrophage gene [gene=GAL3ST4; type=sc_celltype_expression; source=DATASET:LI2022-SCRNA; cell_group=Macrophage; tissue=tumor; share_of_tumor_transcripts=0.972] whose bulk rise shrinks at full purity [gene=GAL3ST4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.401], and higher expression goes with worse survival [gene=GAL3ST4; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.177]. LILRB4 is flagged infiltration-driven, with its signal largely vanishing at full purity [gene=LILRB4; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=0.508]. None of the discovery candidates is a selective dependency.

validation.text: The independent layers strengthen CA9, NNMT and CD70. CA9 stays strongly tumour-up when extrapolated to a pure tumour [gene=CA9; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=7.787]. CD70 also survives the purity check [gene=CD70; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=4.278] after a large TCGA rise [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.0902]. NNMT has a prognostic association with shorter survival [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; padj=0.0048] and confirmatory-cohort protein replication [gene=NNMT; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=3.07e-46]. SCARB1 protein also replicates [gene=SCARB1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=2.334], but its cell of origin does not.

The same layers weaken other candidates. HK2 is the clearest case: its discovery protein increase [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_discovery_log2fc=2.106] does not replicate in the confirmatory cohort [gene=HK2; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_padj=0.074]. None of the tumour-up candidates (CA9, CD70, ENPP3, SCARB1, NNMT) is a ccRCC cell-line dependency. EPAS1 is the only selective dependency, with a minority of ccRCC lines dependent [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; frac_ccrcc_dependent=0.208]. VHL is the only recurrent somatic driver among the reviewed genes. The PSAT1 and PCK1 protein losses replicate, but the single PSAT1 phosphosite does not.

robustness.text: Under random re-weighting of the evidence streams, a small set of calls is stable. In the target profile, SCARB1 [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=8], CA9 [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.941], SLC16A3 [gene=SLC16A3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881], CD70 and NNMT [gene=NNMT; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.954] and ENPP3 [gene=ENPP3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.823] stay near the top. In the biomarker profile, PSAT1 [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=4] and PCK1 [gene=PCK1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.889] are the robust calls.

Other positions depend on the chosen weights. ALDH6A1 can reach the top of the biomarker profile but has a wide interval [gene=ALDH6A1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=33]. ALDOB, second in the overall convergence ranking, is often outside the biomarker top twenty-five once weights vary [gene=ALDOB; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top25=0.486]. In the overall convergence ranking only CA9 is a robust top-ten call, so the overall score should not be read as a fixed ordering.

treatment.text: In IMmotion150, no reviewed candidate shows a significant association with outcome, and no gene separates the two main arms after correction. Higher CA9 expression is associated with longer benefit on sunitinib [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.log_hr_per_sd=-0.336], but the adjusted p-value is not significant [gene=CA9; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.sunitinib.padj=0.332]. Higher PCK1 points towards earlier progression on atezolizumab plus bevacizumab [gene=PCK1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab_bevacizumab.padj=0.572]. NNMT and PSAT1 have only small or single-arm results [gene=PSAT1; type=treatment_response; source=IMmotion150 and Choueiri 2016 treatment-response trials (cBioPortal datahub); arms.atezolizumab.padj=0.829]. These are association leads, not predictive biomarkers.

subtypes.text: CA9 is the only reviewed candidate flagged as a subgroup candidate, for PBRM1-mutant tumours. The flag is driven by RNA [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_rna.mutant_minus_wildtype_log2=0.971], while the protein difference does not reach significance [gene=CA9; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; PBRM1.cptac_protein.padj=0.067]. PSAT1 and PCK1 are not subgroup candidates for VHL, PBRM1, BAP1 or SETD2. PCK1 has a strong ccA/ccB difference in TCGA RNA [gene=PCK1; type=subtype_profile; source=CPTAC and TCGA-KIRC tumours split by driver mutation and ccA/ccB; ccA_ccB.tcga_rna.ccB_minus_ccA_log2=-2.581] that is absent at protein level. Mutation-group comparisons rest on few mutant cases and can reflect infiltration differences, so these are hypotheses for stratified studies.

adc.text: For an antibody-drug conjugate or radioligand, CD70 scores highest [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746], but it has no normal-tissue staining data, so its safety cannot be judged. CA9 is a good known control [gene=CA9; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.647] with stomach staining and patchy expression in some tumours. ENPP3 stains strongly in kidney and duodenum. SCARB1 is expressed in few tumour cells in the weakest donors [gene=SCARB1; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=7.1%]. SLC16A3 has the most even expression [gene=SLC16A3; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; tumour_cells_expressing_pct_weakest_quarter_of_donors=43.7%], but as a multi-pass transporter it exposes little extracellular surface. A high suitability score does not show that a conjugate would work.

immune.text: Immune deconvolution separates infiltration genes from tumour-cell genes. FCGR3A is almost entirely immune-derived [gene=FCGR3A; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.999] and tracks the overall immune score, so it marks hot, infiltrated tumours and serves as a control. CD70 sits in between [gene=CD70; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.654]: it correlates with CD8 T-cell content and has a substantial immune component. NNMT is a tumour-cell gene with negligible immune share [gene=NNMT; type=immune_profile; source=CPTAC CIBERSORT and xCell immune deconvolution; immune_cell_share_of_tumour_transcripts=0.015], so its signal should hold in cold tumours too. The immune-track discovery genes (GAL3ST4, LILRB4) and the literature genes TYROBP and FCER1G belong to this infiltration class.

integration.text: Omics, literature and external knowledge converge most clearly on CA9: tumour-cell protein increase, literature on imaging and targeting, and clinical-stage antibodies. They also converge on CD70 and NNMT, each with one caveat (immune expression for CD70, no drug for NNMT). The layers disagree on SCARB1 and ENPP3, which are strong in omics but absent from the literature corpus, and on EPAS1, which is weak in bulk expression but is the only validated drug target and the only selective dependency. The top of the overall convergence ranking is dominated by tubule-loss biomarkers (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD), which are useful for tissue classification but are not targets. In short, CA9, CD70 and ENPP3 are antigen-delivery targets, NNMT is a combined target and biomarker hypothesis, EPAS1 is the mechanism-validated reference, PSAT1 and PCK1 are biomarkers, and SLC16A3 and SLC2A1 describe mechanism.

targets.rationale: Most robust convergent call: first overall and second in the target profile [gene=CA9; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.941]. It is a tumour-cell-intrinsic surface antigen with replicated single-cell attribution and clinical-stage antibodies. There is no dependency, and patchy expression limits conjugates.

Surface antigen with clinical antibodies and the top conjugate suitability [gene=CD70; type=adc_profile; source=UniProt topology, Human Protein Atlas staining and scRNA homogeneity; suitability=0.746]. It is robust in the target profile and survives the purity check, but it has a substantial immune-cell component and no normal-tissue staining data.

Tumour-cell enzyme whose protein increase replicates in the confirmatory cohort and in a second single-cell dataset, with an adverse survival association [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]. It has no clinical drug and no cell-line dependency, so the target call is a hypothesis.

Placed above its numeric rank because it is the only clinically validated axis (belzutifan) and the only selective ccRCC dependency [gene=EPAS1; type=depmap_dependency; source=DATASET:DEPMAP-26Q1; selectivity=0.3]. Its bulk expression signal is weak and its transcripts are largely non-tumour in single-cell data.

Robust in the target profile [gene=ENPP3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.823], with a clinical-stage conjugate. Strong kidney and duodenum staining and the absence of ccRCC literature in the corpus limit it.

First in the target profile and the most robust there [gene=SCARB1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.968], with replicated protein. Placed below CA9, CD70, NNMT and ENPP3 because its tumour-cell attribution does not replicate across single-cell datasets, it is expressed in few tumour cells in some donors, and it has no drug or dependency.

MCT4 lactate exporter, robust in the target profile [gene=SLC16A3; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:target:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=target; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.881], with even tumour expression. It is better read as part of the glycolytic mechanism, and it exposes little extracellular surface for antibodies.

The most robust biomarker [gene=PSAT1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.p_top10=0.986]. Its protein loss replicates in the confirmatory cohort. It is not a subgroup marker and has no treatment association.

Robust tubule-loss biomarker whose protein loss and both phosphosites replicate [gene=PCK1; type=confirmatory_replication; source=CPTAC ccRCC confirmatory cohort, DIA proteome and phosphoproteome (PDC000411); protein_conf_log2fc=-4.819]. Its RNA ccA/ccB difference is not seen at protein level.

Strong loss of a tubule metabolic enzyme with frequent copy-number loss, but its biomarker-profile position depends on the weights [gene=ALDH6A1; type=analysis_ranking; source=ANALYSIS:ranking:biomarker:8d5ff79b77e8d233; profile=biomarker; rank_interval_90.rank_p95=33].

Exploratory: tumour-cell-derived transmembrane collagen [gene=COL23A1; type=discovery_profile; source=Europe PMC + Open Targets + UniProt + CPTAC + scRNA-seq; track=tumor; source_share=0.881] that replicates in TCGA and survives the purity check, with antibody tractability. Main limitation: no selective dependency, and normal-tissue protein staining and tumour heterogeneity are untested.

Exploratory: tumour-cell Rab GTPase that holds at full purity [gene=RAB42; type=purity; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PURITY; rna_lfc_at_purity1=3.189] and replicates in TCGA. Main limitation: an intracellular GTPase with a doubtful surface annotation and no dependency evidence.

Exploratory: macrophage-derived enzyme with an adverse survival association and the highest structural-context score examined [gene=GAL3ST4; type=structural_context; source=DATASET:ALPHAFOLD-DB; structural_context_score=0.7874], which is a descriptive heuristic. Main limitation: it is a microenvironment gene whose bulk signal largely disappears at full purity, and its function in ccRCC is unvalidated.

limitations.text: Automatic checks establish evidence linkage and numeric bindings only. They do not validate causal interpretations, treatment efficacy or every sentence.
No candidate except EPAS1 shows a selective ccRCC cell-line dependency, so most target calls rest on expression selectivity and antibody, imaging or conjugate delivery.

Bulk tumour-versus-normal comparisons are confounded by loss of normal tubule tissue and by immune and stromal infiltration. Purity extrapolation and single-cell attribution reduce but do not remove this.
The single-cell and spatial datasets cover few donors, and endothelium and fibroblasts are small populations. SCARB1 attribution differs between datasets.
Treatment-response associations come from modest trial arms, and no gene differs between arms after correction.
Discovery candidates are data-ranked hypotheses. Novelty is counted by gene-symbol literature searches, and none of them has functional, staining or dependency validation.
Structural-context scores describe cavities in predicted monomers. They are not evidence of a degron, of ligase compatibility or of degradability.
The literature corpus is a limited set of ccRCC abstracts with sentence-level extraction, so absence of a relation is not evidence of absence.
